players.product: on-premises superconducting quantum computers (five-qubit IQM Spark; IQM Radiance, approximately 20 to 150 qubits) and IQM Resonance cloud

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Jan Kürschner: Q2 2026 revenue was EUR 6.7 million and H1 2026 revenue EUR 8.9 million, generated from quantum computing only and primarily from sales of on-premise systems including the associated service and maintenance; revenue from hardware and services was EUR 6.4 million for Q2 and EUR 8.3 million for the half year; total revenue also includes cloud-based usage of IQM's quantum computers and co-development projects.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 2026 revenue EUR 6.7 million; H1 2026 EUR 8.9 million; hardware and services EUR 6.4 million (Q2), EUR 8.3 million (H1)

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Jan Kürschner: gross margin was 46% for Q2 2026; reported operating loss was EUR 30.9 million for Q2 and EUR 60.5 million for H1 2026, reflecting significant R&D investment; H1 general and admin expenses include EUR 9.9 million of one-time listing costs, with many listing expenses to be recognized in Q3 at closing of the transaction.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 gross margin 46%; operating loss EUR 30.9 million (Q2), EUR 60.5 million (H1); EUR 9.9 million listing costs in H1 G&A

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Jan Kürschner: IQM opened 2026 with an order backlog of EUR 67.3 million, added EUR 10.6 million of order intake in H1 2026 while recognizing EUR 8.9 million of revenue, and ended the half year with an order backlog of EUR 69.1 million; since the end of Q2 the order backlog has grown by another EUR 33 million to over EUR 102 million.
quarterly_data.figure: order backlog EUR 69.1 million at end-H1 2026 (EUR 67.3 million at start of 2026); H1 order intake EUR 10.6 million; over EUR 102 million after a further EUR 33 million since Q2

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Jan Kürschner: confirming full-year 2026 guidance - order intake target EUR 65 million-EUR 75 million and revenue target EUR 42 million-EUR 47 million; the 2026 revenue model is structurally second-half and Q4 heavy.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 order intake target EUR 65 million-EUR 75 million; FY2026 revenue target EUR 42 million-EUR 47 million

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Jan Kürschner: the largest part of IQM's 2026 revenue recognition is scheduled for Q4 2026, tied to the scheduled delivery and customer acceptance milestones of its first 150-qubit system; in H2 IQM is working on the deployment of one or two smaller systems while continuing to build the larger systems to be delivered.
quarterly_data.figure: first 150-qubit system: delivery and customer acceptance scheduled for Q4 2026

quarterly_data.signal: Customer CSC (LUMI AI Factory): CEO Jan Goetz said IQM was selected (announced in early July) to integrate a quantum computer into the LUMI AI Factory at CSC, connected to one of the world's leading supercomputers, a deal recently closed; CFO Jan Kürschner said the LUMI order is another EUR 33 million and brings 2026 order intake to EUR 50 million so far, and that the EUR 65 million-EUR 75 million order intake guidance is on the cautious side but IQM is positive it will make it.
quarterly_data.figure: LUMI order EUR 33 million; 2026 order intake EUR 50 million to date

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Jan Goetz: as of the close of Q2 2026 IQM has cumulatively since inception sold 26 full-stack quantum computers worldwide, built more than 50 quantum computers and delivered 17 systems, with eight systems currently in production (all 26 are final sales to customers, he confirmed in Q&A); four of the top 10 supercomputing centers in the world use IQM full-stack quantum computers.
quarterly_data.figure: 26 systems sold; more than 50 built; 17 delivered; 8 in production

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Jan Goetz: after the initial ramp-up of its proprietary quantum chip fab in Espoo, Finland in 2021, IQM has invested another EUR 40 million in industrial expansion of the factory, doubling its clean room capacity to enable production of up to 30 full-stack quantum computers per year; the fab was built for IQM's own technology development and quantum computers, not to operate as a commercial foundry.
quarterly_data.figure: EUR 40 million fab expansion; capacity up to 30 full-stack quantum computers per year

quarterly_data.signal: Customer Galaxy: CEO Jan Goetz said Galaxy, a space company in Poland, purchased a 54-qubit IQM Radiance R3 system for on-premises installation, one of two recent system sales to enterprise customers.
Customer TOYO Corporation: CEO Jan Goetz said IQM signed an agreement to deliver an IQM Radiance R2 system to TOYO Corporation in Japan, securing its third Asian market footprint.

Customer Oak Ridge National Laboratory: CEO Jan Goetz said IQM delivered a new system, now fully operational, at the U.S. Department of Energy's Oak Ridge National Laboratory in Tennessee, and another customer delivery to CINECA Supercomputing Center in Italy; IQM also completed installations of IQM Spark and IQM Radiance R2 systems at universities in Finland, Germany and Poland, and expanded into Japan and Spain through new customer wins and engagements in H1 2026.

CFO Jan Kürschner: customers are currently mainly scientific and government institutions; two customers are commercial (one in Poland, one in Japan) and the rest are from academia; commercial customers are showing more interest but some are waiting for bigger systems to run commercial applications, and IQM expects the mix to move toward commercial customers in the near future; many orders come from public tenders whose timing is set by each country.

CFO Jan Kürschner: for larger systems the time from order intake to revenue recognition extends to 1.5 to two years (site preparation, high-vacuum testing, on-premise installation and calibration); projects of less than six months - systems up to 54 qubits - are recognized at a point in time on delivery, larger systems over time against project milestones; Q3 is typically slower because of the European summer; asked whether higher ASPs of bigger systems go with higher gross margins, he said that is a fair way of looking at it; IQM is not guiding a growth rate for order intake beyond 2026 but anticipates it to grow as contracts get bigger.
quarterly_data.figure: order-to-revenue 1.5 to two years for larger systems; point-in-time recognition up to 54 qubits

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Jan Goetz: IQM's product line is IQM Spark (on-premises entry system for universities), IQM Radiance (core NISQ on-premises system, configurations from five, 20 and 54 qubits today to 150 qubits), IQM Halocene (next-generation on-premises platform for quantum error correction) and the IQM Resonance cloud, accessed through IQM's own platform or via AWS; Radiance and Halocene can operate as SLURM nodes alongside CPUs and GPUs at supercomputing centers; on-premises installations remain the primary revenue engine while cloud adoption grows gradually.
quarterly_data.figure: Radiance configurations 5, 20 and 54 qubits today to 150 qubits

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Jan Goetz: IQM introduced tile codes and then barbell codes, QLDPC error correction codes for its Constellation topology, which its published analysis shows give up to 1,000 times lower logical error rates at the same physical qubit budget or comparable logical performance with up to 8 times fewer physical qubits; a peer-reviewed PRX Quantum paper reported an IQM processor simultaneously exceeding 99.9% fidelity for single-qubit gates, two-qubit gates and readout; IQM launched IQM Pulla, a unified pulse-level compilation engine.
quarterly_data.figure: up to 1,000 times lower logical error rates or up to 8 times fewer physical qubits; above 99.9% fidelity

quarterly_data.signal: Partner NVIDIA: CEO Jan Goetz said IQM is combining its IQM Halocene system with NVIDIA's NVQLink platform for tighter QPU-GPU integration and has worked with NVIDIA on AI-driven parallel qubit calibration using the NVIDIA Ising open family of AI models.

Partner HPE: CEO Jan Goetz said that at HPE Discover IQM announced a collaboration with HPE to integrate IQM's superconducting quantum computers with HPE Cray HPC infrastructure for hybrid enterprise environments; management said in Q&A that IQM works on the quantum part, partners on the supercomputing part, with an open interface in between.

CEO Jan Goetz: on July 6 IQM acquired selected assets of Quantistry GmbH, a cloud-native AI-powered chemical and material simulation company, gaining a proprietary software platform, application IP and a quantum chemistry and machine learning team.

CFO Jan Kürschner: IQM's cash position was EUR 309.4 million immediately following the listing on July 2, providing a runway to Q2 2028; management said in Q&A that the relative share of cloud revenue is expected to grow as commercial applications become more feasible, while the major part of the business is currently on-premise deployment.
quarterly_data.figure: cash EUR 309.4 million after listing; runway to Q2 2028

connects_to.relationship: IQM QPU access distributed through Amazon Braket (Garnet, Emerald)

contracts.signal: CEO Jan Goetz: IQM has an ecosystem partnership with AWS through a reseller agreement; customers can access the IQM Resonance cloud offering either through IQM's own cloud platform or via AWS.
